title: Canary + Fallback Economics: mini-deck & checklist (prototype)
summary: Compact sales-facing deck and technical checklist that pairs canary rollout steps with quick fallback economics to help platform sellers negotiate pilot SLAs and integration playbooks. Focus: simple knobs, cost delta estimates, canary success thresholds, and templated buyer language.
action_items: Review cost delta table with pricing team (task: OP-PRC-56)
Add final fallback playbook for on-prem customers
Get SRE sign-off on KV-cache warmup timing estimates
body:
Slide 1 — Title: Canary + Fallback Economics (mini-deck prototype)
Speaker note: 90s intro for platform sellers; 3 things we want them to leave with — canary rhythm, fallback options, and a simple cost hit table.

Slide 2 — Why this exists
- Common buyer problem: nervous about model regressions / latency spikes during go-live
- Seller ask: show low-friction mitigations with clear cost/sla tradeoffs
- Outcome: shorten procurement cycles by giving concrete fallback commitments and a repeatable canary checklist
Notes: tie to Dedicated capacity options when buyers ask for predictability.

Slide 3 — Canary rhythm (operational checklist)
- Pre-canary: baseline latency & token distribution capture (7d window)
- Canary window: 2–4 hours, 1% traffic -> 25% -> 50% (observe at each step)
- Metrics to watch: p95 latency, error rate, token throughput, output quality regressions (eval set pass rate)
- Stop criteria: p95 > SLO + 40% or eval pass rate drops > 5%
- Rollback: switch routing policy to fallback model variant (see Slide 5)
Quirks / notes-to-self: auto-scaling can mask regressions — prefer fixed capacity during canary if buyer needs deterministic behavior.

Slide 4 — Quick economic deltas (rules of thumb for buyer conversations)
- Fallback to smaller model (e.g., 30% cheaper): cost delta = ~ -30% tokens * unit price; latency improves but quality may drop on hallucination-prone tasks
- Fallback to higher-availability dedicated pool (reserved): cost delta = +20–50% fixed monthly commitment, reduces p95 variance
- Throttle + batch window increase: reduces per-token CPU cost by ~10–25% depending on request size; increases tail latency modestly
Example: 100k tokens/day at $0.02/token -> baseline $2k/day. Canary fallback to slimmed model reduces token cost by $600/day but expect 3–7% quality drop on generation tasks.
Notes: these are estimates — include pricing team stamp before sending to prospects.

Slide 5 — Fallback playbook (technical choices + buyer-facing promises)
- Fallback A: model-variant switch (same architecture, lower-context length) — promise: maintain functional parity for X features, degrade image/longchain features
- Fallback B: regional routing + burst capacity (serve from alternative region) — promise: <2x latency increase worst-case during failover
- Fallback C: degraded feature mode (disable function-calling / heavy-ranking calls) — promise: revert within 30–60s once stable
Template buyer language: 'During pilot we commit to automated fallback to [variant] if p95 latency exceeds [X]ms for Y minutes; Redwood will notify and escalate.'

Slide 6 — Integration seller cheat snippets
- Quick pitch: 'We run a short canary to protect your users: if performance or quality drops beyond predefined thresholds we automatically route traffic to a tested fallback and notify your SRE.'
- Slack snippet for kickoff: '/remind #infra 2h Canary step 1: observe p95 latency and eval pass rate'
- Security/compliance note for private deployments: include KMS key rotation window in pilot scope

Slide 7 — Example checklist (one-page handout)
- Owner: customer eng / Redwood SE
- Baseline capture: date range, sample size, sample prompts
- Canary schedule: start time, traffic % steps, responsible people, ops contacts
- Fallback mapping: for each trigger -> action, rollback owner, expected customer impact
- Communication plan: notification channels and incident severity levels

Slide 8 — Real-world anecdote (internal)
- Short story: pilot with midmarket search vendor — canary flagged hallucination rate increase after model merge; fallback to slim variant reduced hallucinations, cost dropped 24%, pilot continued and scaled.
- Lesson: having a pre-approved fallback prevents procurement stalls.

Slide 9 — Open questions / TODOs (working)
- Need finalized cost multipliers from pricing for each fallback option (Priya owner)
- Should we standardize a 'fallback SLA' template for contracts? legal input required
- Automate Slack/Teams playbooks to reduce time-to-fallback

Slide 10 — Appendix: quick numbers & graphs to pull in
- p95 distributions pre/post fallback (mock plot placeholder)
- Token cost vs latency for common models (table)
- Canary timeline visual (flow chart)

Raw / scratch notes (for internal use, leave rough)
- Might fold into seller playbook as a 1-pager + one-page tech appendix
- UX idea: console one-click 'start canary' with pre-populated traffic ramps and fallback mapping
- Sales objection expected: 'we can't tolerate any quality regression' -> response: propose staged rollout with conversational QA set and custom rollback thresholds
- JIRA hooks: create INF-xxxx per pilot to track canary metrics and outcomes

Questions for review:
- Rohan: Are the stop criteria conservative enough?
- SRE: Will fixed-capacity during canary be realistic on Dedicated?
- Pricing: confirm delta table before QBR

End of doc.
notes: Tone: sales + ops oriented; intentionally compact. Keep as a living draft. Avoid final pricing numbers here — link to pricing spreadsheet once approved.
